article.body_preview: DHAKA - Economists are fond of drawing analogies from flying. Thus, when economies attain sufficient, sustained growth, they "take off." When external conditions help them grow faster, they are pushed by "tailwinds." Conversely, if unfavourable conditions force them to slow, they face the "headwinds."
